Rashi on Niddah 15a:10:1.hebrew: בשלא גמר ביאתו - ואפילו הכי, לר"ע מטמאה את בועלה, דהעראה בנדה כגמר ביאה, דכתיב (ויקרא כ׳:י״ח) "את מקורה הערה". אבל לענין קרי, עד שיזריע:
Rashi on Niddah 15a:10:1.english: Where he did not complete his act of intercourse - And even so, according to Rabbi Akiva she renders her partner impure, since initial penetration with a menstruating woman is like a completed act of intercourse, as it is written (Leviticus 20:18): "He has laid bare her source." But with regard to a seminal emission, [he is not impure] until he emits seed.

Rashi on Niddah 15a:11:1.hebrew: ור"מ היא - דמחמיר בכתמים, כדאמר בפ"ק (לעיל נדה ה.), ולקמן בפרק בא סימן (נדה דף נב:):
Rashi on Niddah 15a:11:1.english: And it is [the opinion of] Rabbi Meir - For he is stringent regarding blood stains, as stated in the first chapter (above, Niddah 5a), and below in the chapter [entitled] "Bah Siman" (Niddah 52b).

Rashi on Niddah 15a:12:1.hebrew: פשיטא - מאי מודי? הא בלמפרע פליגי, לגבי מעת לעת, ולא במכאן ולהבא:
Rashi on Niddah 15a:12:1.english: Obvious - What is he conceding? Behold, they disagree about retroactively, with regard to [the rule of] a period of day and night, and not about from now and onward.

Rashi on Niddah 15a:13:1.english: And [the impurity of] stains is rabbinic - Even from now onward [i.e., even for the future, the stain does not render the man impure]:

Rashi on Niddah 15a:14:1.hebrew: אין שור שחוט - דאתמול לא חזאי, אלא סייג בעלמא הוא:
Rashi on Niddah 15a:14:1.english: There is no slaughtered ox - For yesterday she did not see [blood]; rather, it is merely a safeguard.

Rashi on Niddah 15a:14:2.hebrew: הכא הרי שור שחוט לפניך - דבצפור לא נתעסקה, ובשוק של טבחים לא עברה, ומיום שלבשתו היא בספק זה:
Rashi on Niddah 15a:14:2.english: Here, behold, the slaughtered ox is before you - For she did not occupy herself with a bird, and did not pass through the butchers' market, and from the day she wore it [the garment] she has been in this doubt.

Rashi on Niddah 15a:16:1.hebrew: כל הנשים בחזקת טהרה לבעליהן - בלא בדיקה, שלא הוזכרה בדיקה אלא לעסוקה בטהרות:
Rashi on Niddah 15a:16:1.english: All women are presumed pure for their husbands - Without examination, for examination is mentioned only [in the case of a woman] who handles pure foods [i.e., teruma and other consecrated items].

Rashi on Niddah 15a:18:1.hebrew: בתוך ימי עונתה - ל' יום לראייה. אבל לאחר ל' בעיא בדיקה, הואיל וסתם נשים חזיין לסוף עונה:
Rashi on Niddah 15a:18:1.english: Within the days of her period - Thirty days from [her previous] sighting [of blood]. But after thirty [days], she requires an examination, since ordinarily women see [blood] at the end of the [thirty-day] period.

Rashi on Niddah 15a:1:1.hebrew: שמא כר"ע אתם אומרים שמטמאה את בועלה - שהיא מטמאה כל מעת לעת, ואין לכם שיעור בדבר אלא מעת לעת:
Rashi on Niddah 15a:1:1.english: Perhaps you say, like Rabbi Akiva, that she renders impure the one who has relations with her - [that she renders impure] for the entire twenty-four-hour period, and you have no measure in the matter other than a twenty-four-hour period:

Rashi on Niddah 15a:1:2.hebrew: לא שמענו - את שיעורו, וכר"א לא סבירא לן:
Rashi on Niddah 15a:1:2.english: We have not heard - its measure; and in accordance with Rabbi Akiva, we do not hold.

Rashi on Niddah 15a:21:1.hebrew: לא שנו - דכי מצאה תוך ימי עונתה, לא בעיא בדיקה:
Rashi on Niddah 15a:21:1.english: They did not teach - For when she found [blood] within the days of her [expected] period, she does not require examination.

Rashi on Niddah 15a:21:2.hebrew: אלא שלא הגיע עת וסתה - בתוך אותן ימים שהיה בדרך, כגון אשה שיש לה וסת ולא הגיע הוסת בתוך אותן הימים:
Rashi on Niddah 15a:21:2.english: Only when the time of her period had not arrived - Within those days that he was on the road; for example, a woman who has a set period, and [the time of her period] did not arrive within those days.

Rashi on Niddah 15a:21:3.hebrew: אבל הגיע עת וסתה - קודם ביאתו מן הדרך:
Rashi on Niddah 15a:21:3.english: But if the time of her period had arrived - before his arrival from the road.

Rashi on Niddah 15a:21:4.english: She is forbidden - For the way [of the period] is that it comes at its [set] time.

Rashi on Niddah 15a:21:5.hebrew: דאורייתא - הלמ"מ, דמחזקינן לה בטומאת ספק:
Rashi on Niddah 15a:21:5.english: By Torah law - [It is] a halakha transmitted to Moses at Sinai, that we presume her [to be] in a state of impurity of doubt.

Rashi on Niddah 15a:22:1.hebrew: וסתות דרבנן - הצריכוה חכמים לבדוק ביום וסתה, שמא תראה. ומיהו, היכא דלא הוה בעיר, ולא ידעינן אי בדקה אי לא בדקה — לא מספקינן לה בטומאה:
Rashi on Niddah 15a:22:1.english: [That] periods [are] rabbinic - The Sages required her to examine herself on the day of her period, lest she see [blood]. However, where [the husband] was not in town, and we do not know whether she examined herself or did not examine herself, we do not [view] her as being in a state of doubtful impurity:

Rashi on Niddah 15a:2:1.hebrew: לא שהתה כדי שתרד - אלא כדי שתשב ותבדוק, ועודה במטה, טמאין מספק, דהיינו אחר אותיום, כרב חסדא:
Rashi on Niddah 15a:2:1.english: She did not wait long enough to descend - but only [long enough] to sit up and examine herself, while she is still on the bed, they are impure due to uncertainty; that is, [this is the case] after the day of intercourse, like Rav Chisda.

Rashi on Niddah 15a:3:1.english: She waited long enough for it to descend - For its measure is substantial.

Rashi on Niddah 15a:3:2.hebrew: אחר הזמן הוא זה - כלומר, "אחר" של המשנה "אחר" הוא זה:
Rashi on Niddah 15a:3:2.english: "After the time" is this - That is to say, [the mishna's] "after" is [this] "after":

Rashi on Niddah 15a:4:1.hebrew: וכן מעת לעת - כלומר, כשיעור הזה ומכאן ולהלן, כל מעת לעת של בעילה, אם בדקה ומצאתה טמאה, בועלה מטמאה משום נוגע במעת לעת בנדה — טומאת ערב, וספק מדרבנן, לתלות — ואינו מטמא משום בועל נדה — טומאת שבעה — ואפילו לתלות:
Rashi on Niddah 15a:4:1.english: And likewise [when she waited] from period to period - That is, with this measure and onward, [in] every twenty-four-hour period after intercourse, if she examined herself and found herself impure, the one who had relations with her becomes impure because of touching [a woman] in the twenty-four-hour period [when she is] a menstruant — [with] impurity until evening, and a doubt of rabbinic origin, in order to attribute [the impurity to the intercourse] — but he does not become impure as one who has relations with a menstruant — [with] seven-day impurity — even in order to attribute [it].

Rashi on Niddah 15a:4:2.english: He enters the Sanctuary - [The Gemara] explains this below.

Rashi on Niddah 15a:5:1.hebrew: בשלמא לרב חסדא - דאמר כדי שתרד, אחר אחר הוא, ולכן היינו דמטהרי רבנן:
Rashi on Niddah 15a:5:1.english: Granted, according to Rav Chisda - who said [the period is] the time it takes for her to descend [from the bed], [any time] after that is a later time [and not connected to the intercourse]; this is why the Rabbis deem [him] pure:

Rashi on Niddah 15a:7:1.hebrew: וכי תימא דאין עד בידה - דאחר שתרד הוצרכה להושיט, דהוה להו תרי שיעורי, א"כ איבעי ליה למיתני ולפלוגי בין עד בידה לאין עד בידה, דלא תיפוק חורבה מיניה. דהשתא משמע דאפילו עד בידה, דלא שהתה אלא כדי שתרד, מטהרי רבנן. ומדלא מפליג ש"מ דודאי מטהרי רבנן בכדי שתרד לחודיה:
Rashi on Niddah 15a:7:1.english: And if you say that there is no cloth in her hand - [That is,] that after she descends she needed to extend [her hand], so that there would be two time-measures — if so, [the tanna] should have taught and distinguished between [a case where] a cloth is in her hand and [a case where] no cloth is in her hand, so that no ruin would come out of it. For now it implies that even [where] a cloth is in her hand, [and] she waited only the time it takes to descend, the Rabbis declare [her] pure. And since [the tanna] did not distinguish, learn from this that the Rabbis certainly declare [her] pure [after] the time it takes to descend alone.

Tosafot on Niddah 15a:11:1.hebrew: אמר רב למפרע ור"מ היא - וא"ת: דבפ"ק דיומא (דף ב.) תנן: מפרישין כ"ג מביתו ז' ימים, דשמא יבא על אשתו ספק נדה; וקאמר: כמאן? כר"ע דאמר אף מטמאה את בועלה. וקאמר רב חסדא דאתי אפילו כרבנן, ובחד אחר מודו דבועלה טמא ז'. אמאי לא משני שמא תמצא כתם? דהא מודים חכמים לר"ע ברואה כתם. וי"ל: משום שמואל דאמר הכא מכאן ולהבא. ועוד י"ל: דהיא תבדוק חלוקה קודם פרישתו, ואז לא נטמא הכהן קודם בדיקה. וא"ת: אמאי קאמר שמא תמצא אשתו ספק נדה? לימא ודאי נדה, אם תבדוק שיעור וסת סמוך לבעילה. וי"ל: דהא לא שכיחא:
Tosafot on Niddah 15a:11:1.english: "Rav said: retroactively, and it is [in accordance with] Rabbi Meir" - And if you say: In the first chapter of Yoma (2a) we learned: They separate the High Priest from his home seven days [before Yom Kippur], lest he engage in intercourse with his wife who is a possible niddah. And [the Gemara] says: Like whom? Like Rabbi Akiva, who said that she even renders impure the man who has intercourse with her. And Rav Chisda said that it can come even [according] to the Rabbis, for with regard to one other [case] they concede that the man who has intercourse with her is impure for seven days. Why does it not answer: lest she find a blood stain? For the Rabbis concede to Rabbi Akiva regarding a woman who sees a blood stain. And one can answer: Because of Shmuel, who said here [that it is] from now on [only]. And furthermore, one can answer: That she would examine her garment before his separation, and then the priest would not have become impure before the examination. And if you say: Why does it say "lest his wife be found a possible niddah"? Let it say "a definite niddah," if she examines [herself] for the length of a veset close to intercourse. And one can answer: That is not common:

Tosafot on Niddah 15a:21:1.hebrew: הכי איתמר לא שנו אלא שלא הגיע שעת וסתה - לא היה לו לחזור ממה שאמר תחלה "לא שנו אלא שאין לה וסת", דאמת הוא דהיא בחזקת טהרה, כדאמרינן בפ"ק (לעיל נדה יב.): כל לבעלה לא בעיא בדיקה, אפילו אין לה וסת. והיה יכול להוסיף: ויש לה וסת נמי, כשלא הגיע שעת וסתה כו'. אלא שהגמרא מיישב הלשון שאמר תחלה בלא תוספת:
Tosafot on Niddah 15a:21:1.english: "This is how it was stated: They taught [this] only when the time of her period had not arrived" - He [Rav Huna] should not have retracted from what he said at first, "They taught [this] only when she has no set period," for it is true that she is presumed to be pure, as we said in the first chapter (above, Niddah 12a): A woman [who is permitted] to her husband does not require examination, even if she has no set period. And he could have added: "And [the same applies if] she has a set period too, when the time of her period had not arrived," etc. Rather, [the Gemara] reconciles the wording that he stated at first without any addition:

Tosafot on Niddah 15a:22:1.hebrew: אפי' הגיע זמן וסתה מותרת - תימה: היאך מותרת? הא אמרינן בשבועות פ"ב (דף יח:) ולקמן פרק האשה (נדה דף סג:): אזהרה לבני ישראל שיפרשו מנשותיהן סמוך לוסתן! וי"ל: כששהתה אחר וסתה שבעה ימים שיכולה לטבול איירי, דספק טבילה מוציאה מידי ספק ראתה, כההוא דר' יוחנן דבסמוך. ולמ"ד וסתות דאורייתא, אפילו שהתה כשיעור זמן טבילה אסורה, דודאי ראתה חשבינן לה. ומתוך כך יש לדקדק דס"ל לרבי יוחנן דבסמוך וסתות דרבנן:
Tosafot on Niddah 15a:22:1.english: Even if the time of her period arrived, she is permitted - It is astonishing: How is she permitted? Surely we said in Shevuot, chapter 2 (18b), and later in the chapter [entitled] HaIshah (Niddah 63b): "It is a warning to the Children of Israel that they should separate from their wives near their [expected] period!" And one can answer: [The Gemara] is speaking where she waited seven days after her period, [so that] she is able to immerse, for the uncertainty of immersion removes [her] from the uncertainty of whether she saw [blood], like that [case] of Rabbi Yochanan shortly below. But according to the one who says that periods [are in force] by Torah law, even if she waited the amount of time [needed] for immersion she is forbidden, for we consider her as having definitely seen [blood]. And from this one can infer that Rabbi Yochanan, [mentioned] shortly below, holds that periods are by rabbinic law:

Tosafot on Niddah 15a:2:1.hebrew: לא שהתה כדי שתרד מן המטה מטמאה את בועלה [וחייבת באשם תלוי] שהתה כדי שתרד כו' ר"ע אומר מטמאה בועלה - תימה: אי ר"ע מודה ברישא, כדמשמע דלא פליג אלא אסיפא, א"כ סבר יש אם למסורת! ובפ"ק דסנהדרין (דף ד.) אית ליה לר"ע יש אם למקרא, גבי רביעית דם הבא משני מתים, דקאמר: נפשות קרינן. וליכא למימר דהכא פליג נמי ברישא, דהתנן פ' דם שחיטה (כריתות דף כב:): בחתיכה של קודש וחתיכה של חולין, אכל אחד את הראשונה ובא אחר ואכל את השניה — זה מביא אשם תלוי וזה מביא אשם תלוי, דברי ר"ע. ואמאי חייב השני? הא בשעה שאכל לא היו לפניו ב' חתיכות, ולמאן דבעי ב' חתיכות פטור בכה"ג, כדאמר התם בסוף פרקין. ורבי נמי אית ליה בפ' ספק אכל (שם דף יח.), היכא דאכל את הראשונה במזיד והשניה בשוגג, דחייב אשם תלוי על השניה; ורבי סבר בפ"ק דסנהדרין (דף ד.) יש אם למקרא. וצ"ל דיש שום חילוק בין מקרא למסורת: זה למקרא ומסורת דעלמא. דחייא בר רב דבעי ב' חתיכות סבר דכ"ע סברי הכא דיש אם למקרא, ורב אסי דפליג עליה סבר דכ"ע סברי יש אם למסורת, כמו שמצינו (ב"מ דף כב:) גבי יותן דומיא דיתן, ועובד דומיא דעבד (פסחים דף כו:), ועוני דומיא דעני (שם לו.), וכפות דומיא דכפת (סוכה דף לב.), והתם יש טעמא אחרינא. ותדע, דכי פריך התם טובא לחייא בר רב, ומשני: ר"א היא דמחייב אשם תלוי על חלב כוי, והא כמה תנאי פליגי במקרא ובמסורת, ואמאי נקט טפי ר"א? דשמותי הוא. וגם המקשה, וכי לא הוה ידע דטובא תנאי פליגי במקרא ובמסורת? אלא כדפרישית. ועוד י"ל דר"ע ורבי איירו דהראשון לא אכל כל החתיכה אלא חציה, וכשאכל השניה היו עדיין ב' החתיכות לפניו. וכענין זה מתרץ הירושלמי בהאשה רבה:
Tosafot on Niddah 15a:2:1.english: "[If] she did not wait long enough to descend from the bed, she renders impure the man who had relations with her [and she is obligated to bring a provisional guilt offering]. [If she waited] long enough to descend, etc. Rabbi Akiva says she renders impure the man who had relations with her" - This is difficult: If Rabbi Akiva agrees in the first clause, as it implies that he disagrees only with the latter clause, then he holds that "there is a basis for the oral reading [of a verse]"! Yet in the first chapter of Sanhedrin (4a) Rabbi Akiva holds that "there is a basis for the written reading," regarding a quarter-log of blood from two corpses, where he says: "We read [the verse as] 'souls.'" And one cannot say that here he disagrees in the first clause as well, for we learned in the chapter [entitled] Dam Shechitah (Keritot 22b): [In the case of] a piece [of meat] of sacred food and a piece of unconsecrated food, [if] one person ate the first and another came and ate the second — this one brings a provisional guilt offering and that one brings a provisional guilt offering; [these are] the words of Rabbi Akiva. But why is the second liable? When he ate, there were not two pieces before him, and according to the one who requires two pieces, he is exempt in such a case, as it says there at the end of the chapter. And Rabbi [Yehudah HaNasi] also holds, in the chapter [entitled] Safek Achal (ibid. 18a), that where one ate the first intentionally and the second unwittingly, he is liable for a provisional guilt offering for the second; yet Rabbi holds in the first chapter of Sanhedrin (4a) that "there is a basis for the written reading." So one must say that there is some distinction between the written reading and the oral reading: this [case] is [about] the written reading, and [that of Sanhedrin is] about the oral reading in general. [That is,] Chiya bar Rav, who requires two pieces, holds that everyone here agrees that "there is a basis for the written reading," while Rav Assi, who disagrees with him, holds that everyone agrees that "there is a basis for the oral reading," as we find (Bava Metzia 22b) regarding yutan [being read] like yitan, and ovad like avad (Pesachim 26b), and oni like ani (ibid. 36a), and kafut like kafat (Sukkah 32a); and there, there is another reason. And know [that this is so], for when [the Gemara] there raises many objections against Chiya bar Rav, and answers: It is Rabbi Eliezer who holds one is liable for a provisional guilt offering for the fat of a koy — but many Tannaim disagree about the written and the oral reading, so why did it choose Rabbi Eliezer in particular? [Because] he is of the school of Shammai. And also the questioner — did he not know that many Tannaim disagree about the written and the oral reading? Rather, [it is] as I explained. Furthermore, one may say that Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi [Yehudah HaNasi] are speaking of a case where the first [person] did not eat the entire piece but only half of it, so that when he ate the second, the two pieces were still before him. And along these lines the Yerushalmi resolves [it] in [the chapter] HaIshah Rabbah:

Tosafot on Niddah 15a:7:1.hebrew: האי עד בידה ואין עד בידה מיבעי ליה - פרש"י דה"ל לפלוגי הכל בשהתה. וקשה, דלמא מפליג בדידה באין עד בידה בין שהתה ללא שהתה? ונראה לפרש דה"ל לפרושי בברייתא באין עד בידה, כיון דמתניתין איירי ביש עד בידה:
Tosafot on Niddah 15a:7:1.english: "This: 'a cloth is in her hand,' and 'a cloth is not in her hand' — it should have said" - Rashi explained that it should have distinguished everything [by saying] "if she waited." But this is difficult: perhaps it distinguishes within that very case, [where] a cloth is not in her hand, between [where] she waited and [where] she did not wait? It appears to explain that it should have specified in the baraita [the case where] a cloth is not in her hand, since the Mishnah is dealing with [the case where] a cloth is in her hand:

Tosafot on Niddah 15a:9:1.hebrew: כשמאי דאמר דיה שעתה - ומ"מ מודה שמאי בחד אחר, דטמא שבעה, כיון דחייב אשם תלוי:
Tosafot on Niddah 15a:9:1.english: Like Shammai, who said: Her time is sufficient - And nevertheless, Shammai concedes in one other case, that she is impure for seven days, since she is liable for a provisional guilt-offering.
